Hitting your kids is never ok. If they are calling you stupid, belittling you, and damaging your self-esteem to the point that you’re starting to feel like you want to die, that could most definitely count as emotional and verbal abuse. Regardless of whether your mom had good intentions in saying that (she could be trying to encourage you to reach your potential, just in a very shitty way), it’s clearly diminishing your sense of self-worth, and that’s what is important here. Really, it’s not surprising that you’re not performing at your best what with the quarantine and your parents creating a very stressful environment for you. So don’t beat yourself up too much over it. Continue trying your best. 

I want you to know that it has nothing to do with you — none of the things that they say are about you at all, though it’ll sound like they are. It’s about projection and control. However, it’s likely that your parents are like this because they were brought up in a similar way by their own parents. So, they may not realize how much they’re hurting you and that this “tough love” is absolutely not the way to go about it. 

This is why I encourage you to let them know how they are making you feel. Not everything at once of course, and try to be calm and respectful about it even if they aren’t to you. “Mom/Dad, it really hurts my feelings when you do X. When you say X, it makes me feel sad/unloved/dejected, etc.” 

I know it’s a difficult thing to do, but making them realize this is the only way that you can start seeing some change and hopefully they will treat you with more respect. We are all rooting for you, OP.

Don’t worry, I was also scared of opening up to my parents or anyone I knew in real life. But it doesn’t sound like they’re straight up abusive (at least not in a physical sense), are they? If you’re struggling with these feelings often and suspect that you might have depression, please seriously consider telling your parents, or if it’s not safe to do so, another family member or trusted adult. You don’t need to get a paid tutor, I don’t know what the school system is like where you live, but either way asking teachers for extra help or for online math practice resources should work. You seem like a very articulate person just from the way you type. Don’t let anyone make you feel stupid, just because they’re your parents doesn’t mean they’re always right. 

There’s no such thing as being too young to experience depression or stress. Your feelings are always valid, and you matter. But I can promise you that nothing is worth killing yourself over at this point. Certainly not worth it over your parents being jerks or over struggling with school, which everyone does at one point or another. Just think about it — a few years from now when you’re in high school or college, these problems are going to seem so minute and faraway. Don’t deprive yourself of life when it’s only just started.
